prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional small molecules that bring a chosen protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from B034 (Buchwald and Hartwig) to B019, PROTAC-style targeted protein degradation, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. My reasons are scientific. Round 1 showed me that my own case for C-N coupling rested mainly on utility, and the committee's replies (Linke, Aqvist, Zou) sharpened the real weakness: the catalytic cycle and the metal were recognised in 2010, so the amination is a very good ligand-design extension of a recognised principle rather than a new one. B019 is different in kind. A heterobifunctional molecule that forces a neo-interaction between a target and an E3 ligase turns a biological process into a designable chemical event, and the chemistry that made it work is real medicinal and synthetic chemistry: ligand and linker design, rational optimisation of ternary-complex cooperativity, and Ciulli's VHL ligands, which converted the early peptide-based proof of concept into drug-like molecules. Crews and Deshaies supply the concept and first demonstrations, and Ciulli supplies the step that made it a general, reproducible design method that many independent laboratories now use on many targets. I accept Aili's and Aqvist's argument that regulatory approval is not the committee's criterion when the principle has been independently reproduced and is already in late-stage trials. I keep the PROTAC citation separate from the molecular-glue strand because heterobifunctional design and cereblon biology are two partly distinct discoveries, and one honest three-person citation cannot cover both.
statement.case_against: The main weakness is attribution. A PROTAC-only citation leaves out Handa, whose identification of cereblon explained thalidomide and put degraders into the clinic, and four members have chosen Handa as third name; it also leaves out Sakamoto, whose first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies is a priority claim I cannot settle from the supplied material. The first PROTAC used a poorly permeable peptide ligand, so the drug-like version came later, which is why I credit Ciulli. No degrader is approved as far as I know, so the prize would rest on mechanism and reproduced principle rather than a delivered medicine. Finally, my own chemical-novelty question is only partly answered: the new thing is a design principle, not a new reaction, and I accept that as sufficient but others could reasonably not. If the committee prefers a mature, synthetic-methods prize, B034 remains the better-documented candidate and I would still support it.

responses.point: The novelty is a design principle (a bifunctional molecule creates a neo-interaction), and approval is a useful signal but not the criterion for a chemistry prize.
responses.response: You and Dr. Zou have moved me on both points. I asked what was new chemically, and a molecule whose linker and ligand optimisation controls cooperative ternary-complex formation is a chemical answer even without a new reaction. On approval, replication by many independent laboratories and a change in drug-discovery practice are the tests I apply to any method, and B019 meets them. Where I still differ is your trio. Handa's cereblon work is a strong mechanistic discovery, but it is a second achievement, and putting it in a PROTAC citation risks a sentence that is too broad and a credit line that follows the clinical story rather than the chemistry. I would take Ciulli for the step that made PROTACs rational and drug-like.

responses.point: A clean PROTAC prize anchored on Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, whose rational-design chemistry connects mechanism to experiment, and whose citation stays inside the three-laureate limit.
responses.response: I now join you on the configuration. Your round-1 comment on B034 was fair: the amination extends the cross-coupling recognised in 2010, and the weight I put on utility alone did not separate it from other widely used methods. I agree the trio is defensible and that Ciulli's VHL ligands are what turned the early peptide PROTAC into a general design method. I still hold that the Handa objection is real, and I would not call it settled by the three-name limit alone. My answer to the chair's question is that the third name is Ciulli if the citation is PROTAC-only, and Handa only if the committee writes the glue strand into the citation and accepts a broader sentence.

responses.point: Buchwald-Hartwig amination is a mature extension of palladium cross-coupling recognised in 2010, whereas degradation opens a new modality, and B034 could stay in contention for a later year.
responses.response: This is the argument that decided it for me. I had treated three decades of confirmation as the test, but the committee has to ask what is new relative to what has been recognised, and ligand design that made one cross-coupling variant routine is a refinement of the 2010 principle in a way that induced proximity is not of anything earlier. I also take your own maturity reservation seriously, so I would not hide it: the case rests on reproduced mechanism and late-stage trials. Your citation names the principle rather than the modality, which I like, but I would keep it limited to heterobifunctional degraders so that it does not promise credit to the cereblon strand that three names cannot deliver.

responses.point: The novelty is a design principle, not a new reaction, and you rank B034 outside your top eight because the 2010 prize covers the same transformation class and Kosugi's earlier work clouds priority.
responses.response: I accept both parts of your reply. On priority, the Kosugi and Migita aminostannane couplings are real precursors that I could not weigh from the supplied text, and that uncertainty alone is a reason not to build a two-name citation around B034 this year. Your structural point also helps B019: crystal structures of ternary complexes show how cooperativity arises, which is where the chemistry of linker and ligand design actually acts. I disagree only with the cereblon part of your citation. Handa's discovery is excellent, but the chair's question about whether PROTACs and glues are one achievement or two has, in my view, the answer two, and a three-name trio should honour one of them cleanly.

responses.point: Eight credited names across two discoveries (heterobifunctional design versus cereblon as thalidomide target) cannot be honestly compressed into three without ignoring one strand, and the expert reports should show whether the contributions can be separated.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of the problem, and my configuration is my answer to it: I take the heterobifunctional strand and say openly that the molecular-glue arm is left out. I would not support a mixed citation. A two-part prize does not solve the problem because the three-person cap would leave a single name for each part, which would be even less defensible for the PROTAC arm. I note you ranked B019 seventh at the opening and still list it as an alternative; if your doubt is the PROTAC and glue split, a PROTAC-only citation addresses it directly.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a PROTAC-only citation that leaves out Handa and the cereblon strand, which four members put in their trio.
Priority between Sakamoto, Crews and Deshaies for the first PROTAC, and how much Ciulli's VHL ligand work should weigh against it; the supplied material does not settle this.
Whether durable clinical efficacy matters before recognition; I treat reproduced mechanism and late-stage trials as enough but hold this with moderate confidence.
Whether B034 is distinct enough from the 2010 prize and from the Kosugi and Migita precursors to compete in a later year.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal to disclose. I have no recorded tie to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa, Buchwald or Hartwig. My Masamune lineage and my Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr remain collegial links only, not a basis for recusal, and my change of preference was not coordinated with them.
